decision_reason: This is a public and actively maintained MIT-licensed R package of genomics utilities, but it is explicitly a disparate, experimental collection for its author’s daily or occasional work. It has install instructions and package manuals, but no tagged/versioned release or independent scientific/adoption record was found. Hold until an agency-supported reusable package/release or documented operational use beyond the maintainer is established.

government_provenance.note: The package DESCRIPTION names Sebastien Cunnac at an ird.fr address as author and maintainer; the repository is in the PHIM namespace. CIRAD’s official PHIM unit page identifies the joint unit’s regulators as CIRAD, INRAE, IRD, Institut Agro, and University of Montpellier. This supports the maintainer’s institutional relationship, not government adoption of the package.

public_source.note: The project is public and includes an installable R package structure: DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R source, tests, function manuals, and configuration/tool recipes.

eligible_license.note: The direct root LICENSE is the full MIT grant, copyright Sebastien Cunnac (2024); DESCRIPTION also declares MIT. No conflicting code-level notice was found. This pass applies to the package-authored material, not the separately installed bioinformatics tools.

primary_evidence.note: The package describes a disparate set of functions used by the maintainer in daily/occasional genomics work and has man pages plus `remotes::install_git` guidance. It is actively changed (through 2026-07) but has no tags/releases, and I found no documented independent or published use of this exact package; notability/reusable-product status remains unresolved.

product_identity: genomicsR, a personal R package of genomics utilities

family_note: A general genomics R utility library, not a specific pipeline/application identified by one of its function groups. Do not infer that external tools listed in environment recipes inherit the package license.
status_note: The repository existed before 2024, but its full MIT grant was first added by the cited commit; the DESCRIPTION SPDX-style field alone is not used to backdate the explicit grant. Current DESCRIPTION version is 0.0.6998. Clearance path: a versioned public distribution with user guidance, or a primary source showing exact genomicsR use/adoption outside the maintainer’s personal functions collection.

public_source.note: The public project exposes R training Quarto/HTML lessons, images, and class materials.

eligible_license.note: The direct grant is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for educational materials, not an OSI-approved software license for a software product.

primary_evidence.note: The README explicitly identifies the files as teaching material for the CIBiG 2024 R module; the tree contains lessons and slide/course content, not a reusable R software product.

status_note: Rejected for product scope and license class. The CIBiG course and its institutional partnership are verified, but this repository contains lessons, not software.

decision_reason: The public Forge project contains a GPLv3 Snakemake structural-annotation pipeline, but its README directs users to clone a separate GitHub repository (`FlorianCHA/AssemblyAndAnnotation_pipeline`) that now returns 404. I could not establish that upstream’s source/license history is identical to this PHIM copy, or find direct CIRAD/IRD sponsorship, a versioned release, independent scientific use, or current support. Hold pending exact source lineage and institutional/product evidence.

No direct official body page or code notice ties this exact workflow to CIRAD/IRD ownership or deployment; group placement alone is insufficient.

primary_evidence.note: The README describes Snakemake installation and supported tools, but its clone command points to a 404 GitHub repository. decision_reason: The public Snakemake pipeline has a direct GPLv3 grant and an exact CIRAD research-use record: the 2023 ICPP abstract says EffiCAZ was used to improve functional annotation of pathogenicity-related effectors and CAZymes. Hold because its source has no release/versioned distribution, its README is only a one-line description, and the repository has had no activity since 2023; no current product-specific support/use signal was found.

government_provenance.note: The source lead is in CIRAD’s joint PHIM unit namespace. The exact 2023 CIRAD conference abstract names EffiCAZ and CIRAD-affiliated authors (including Sébastien Ravel), tying the pipeline to CIRAD research rather than relying on the repository group name alone.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Snakemake file, configuration, shell launcher, and analysis scripts.

eligible_license.note: The direct root grant is the complete GNU GPL version 3 text; no “or later” option is stated, so this is conservatively recorded as GPL-3.0-only. External tools/databases invoked by the workflow retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: This exact CIRAD conference abstract reports EffiCAZ use in a study of two banana pathogens, satisfying a historical scientific-use pathway. However, the repository has no release/tag and no activity after 2023; there is no current product-specific support/distribution/use signal for the maintained exception.

decision_reason: PodiumASM is a distinct, documented Snakemake genome-assembly quality pipeline with a 1.0.0 tag, direct GPLv3 option, CIRAD authorship, and exact scientific use in a CIRAD 2023 study.
